messages:
Mira: quick heads up — canary run of the new fused-attn kernel shows lower medians but a nasty p99 tail for short-chat traffic. dumping notes here.

Alex: paste the numbers when you have them. :eyes:

Mira: baseline before change: p95=115ms p99=210ms gpu_util=76%
canary (fused-attn): p95=102ms p99=480ms gpu_util=91%
KV cache hit-rate (canary slice): 95% -> 86%

Chao: that gap screams scheduling jitter + more cache misses. fused-attn probably reduces compute but increases start-up variance for small microbatches.

Sanjay: agree. possible factors: kernel launch amortization, different CUDA stream behavior, or our prefetch cadence not matching the new exec schedule. Need per-request breakdown.

Mira: short perf excerpt from a canary pod (replay trace):
```
[2026-03-16T09:12:01Z] req_id=aa3 batch=5 seq=16 kernel=fused-attn-v3 exec_ms=1.1 enqueue_wait_ms=22.8 kv_lookup_ms=8.7 kvcache_miss
[2026-03-16T09:12:02Z] req_id=aa4 batch=3 seq=6  kernel=fused-attn-v3 exec_ms=0.5 enqueue_wait_ms=49.2 kv_lookup_ms=11.3 kvcache_miss
[2026-03-16T09:12:03Z] req_id=aa5 batch=10 seq=64 kernel=fused-attn-v3 exec_ms=3.9 enqueue_wait_ms=12.1 kv_lookup_ms=2.1 kvcache_hit
```

Alex: enqueue_wait spikes line up with p99. When arrivals are bursty small batches sit waiting and the kernel overhead dominates. That explains lower medians (when batches are favorable) and worse tails (when bursts produce many small microbatches).

Chao: mitigation options: bump batching window (trade: higher median), cap microbatch size to avoid pathological boundaries, or do per-seq preferred-kernel routing. Also we could add a short-term p99-based heuristic: if recent p99 > baseline*2, revert to legacy kernel for X minutes.

Sanjay: we should instrument kvcache prefetch vs kernel start time. Hypothesis: fused-attn reorders work across streams so prefetcher misses its timing, increasing miss-rate and miss-latency. Can someone run kvcache latency histograms for canary pods?

Mira: ran a quick scoped metric: median kvcache lookup ~8ms, but 95th ~48ms on canary. Miss rate concentrated on small-seq requests.

perf-bot: perf dashboard: https://perf.redwood/internal/dashboards/canary/189000 — shows p99 overlay and kvcache miss maps

Alex: propose immediate canary rollback. For the next A/B: fused-attn for seq>=24, legacy for seq<24. Also reduce batching window from 60ms -> 35ms for the canary to see impact on enqueue_wait.

Chao: add admission control rule too: if gpu_util > 90% and p99 uplift detected, probabilistic shed new microbatches with p=0.25 and route to smaller-capacity fallback model. That should reduce tail risk at modest throughput cost.

Sanjay: need numbers. Run a shed simulation with traffic replay: 0.25 shed target; measure throughput delta and p99 improvement. If throughput loss <7% and p99 improves by >=2x, we can consider enabling adaptive shedding.

Mira: I'll run the replay+shed sim this afternoon (seq distribution + kvcache patterns). Will attach result summary. For now rolling back fused-attn on canary.

Alex: follow-ups / owners: 1) p99-aware kernel fallback heuristic (Chao), 2) kvcache-miss delta alert (Mira), 3) shed-sim job + results (Sanjay). Please post experiment logs and config diffs in the thread.

Mira: assigned. will post results and a short runbook note for kernel-fallback. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2138 created: p99 regression during fused-attn canary. Severity: low (rollback in place). https://inc.redwood/INC-2138

Alex: good quick rollback. Keep the incident note concise so search surfaces the kernel-fallback rationale.

Chao: extra thought — we should add a lightweight end-to-end microbenchmark that mixes bursty arrival patterns and kvcache-uniformity. That will catch these scheduling mismatches earlier in CI.

Mira: agreed. adding a microbench ticket to backlog.

Sanjay: after we get shed-sim numbers, we can tune probability and thresholds. Leaning to a conservative default shed_prob=0.15 and gpu_util_threshold=0.9, then auto-escalate if p99 still high.

Alex: sounds good. keep updates short here. thanks everyone.
